title: Swanson's magnesium and migraine
question: Which nutritional factors might plausibly be involved in migraine and serve as a preventive target?
known_answer: In 1988 Swanson listed eleven indirect connections between magnesium and migraine drawn from literatures that didn't cite each other, among them vascular tone, spreading cortical depression and calcium-channel effects. He proposed magnesium deficiency as a factor in migraine. Placebo-controlled trials of oral magnesium for prophylaxis followed in the 1990s.
expected_hypothesis: Magnesium deficiency may contribute to migraine, and magnesium supplementation may reduce migraine frequency.
references: Swanson DR. Migraine and magnesium: eleven neglected connections. Perspect Biol Med. 1988;31(4):526-557.

Peikert A, Wilimzig C, Köhne-Volland R. Prophylaxis of migraine with oral magnesium: results from a prospective, multi-center, placebo-controlled and double-blind randomized study. Cephalalgia. 1996;16(4):257-263.
traps: Finding only one of the eleven links and overstating it
